chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, raising it, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

Abu Hanifa came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I saw your son Musa (peace be upon him) praying while people were passing in front of him, and he did not stop them, and what is in it.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Call Musa for me.' So he was called, and he said to him, 'O my son! Abu Hanifa mentions that you were praying while people were passing in front of you, and you did not forbid them.'
He said, 'Yes, O father! The One Whom I was praying to was closer to me than them. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Saying: And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.'
So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) embraced him to himself, then said, 'O my son! By my father and my mother, O the mine of the secrets!'
And this is an education from him (peace be upon him), not that he neglected the merit.

key_terms.أَبُو حَنِيفَة: Abu Hanifa, the prominent Sunni jurist
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, title of Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْفَضْل: Merit/excellence (in the context of prayer rulings)
key_terms.حَبْلُ الْوَرِيد: The jugular vein, used in Quran to denote extreme closeness
key_terms.يَمُرُّونَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ: Passing in front of him (during prayer)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Musa al-Kazim not stop people from passing in front of him during prayer?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) responds to Abu Hanifa’s critique by clarifying that his inaction was not a neglect of the ruling of *sadd al-dhara'i* (blocking the path), but rather a demonstration of deep spiritual presence (*hudhur al-qalb*). By citing the Quranic verse regarding Allah's closeness, he illustrates that for the devout, the awareness of the Divine supersedes the physical distraction of passersby. This hadith is traditionally interpreted by Shia scholars as an example of *tadib* (gentle pedagogical correction) rather than a contradiction of fiqh, emphasizing that the Imam’s practice was rooted in superior spiritual realization.

en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father in a marfu’ manner from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Once, abu Hanifah went to see abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. On his arrival he said, ‘I saw your son Musa perform Salah (prayer) while people passed by in front of him; but he did not stop them and it is questionable.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked to call Musa. He was called and he asked, ‘Son, abu Hanifah says that you were performing Salah (prayer) and people passed by in front of you, but you did not stop them.’

He replied, ‘Yes, O father, the One for whom I was performing Salah (prayer) was closer to me than people passing by in front of me. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, “We are closer to him than the jugular vein.’” [50:16]
The narrator has said that he (the Imam) then embraced him and then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep me and my mother in service for your cause, O reservoir of secrets.’
(Imam’s response is to show the significance of Salah (prayer) not to compromising any excellence.)”
